meta.title: Master · Part 4 · Key word transformation
meta.provenance: From the pantry drafts part4.js and part4b.js (sets 4 and 2; part4c.js was empty and part4d.js repeated part4.js). Reviewed item by item in October 2026: two answers that marked wrong English as right removed (in my point of view; no interest in, which changes the meaning), one honest answer added (so long as). Each answer is "first half|second half": one mark per half, as in the exam. October 2026: 160 transformations added, written new for this app from the patterns of a school set (2005): each keeps its key word and grammar pattern in a fresh situation. A dozen items whose original answers broke the key-word rule were rebuilt, and repeated key words were varied.

items.s: I started learning the guitar five years ago.
items.why: Present perfect continuous with for.

items.s: The last time I saw Mia was in 2019.
items.why: Present perfect negative + since.

items.s: I have never been to Rome before.
items.why: This is my first + noun.

items.s: They began building the house in March and are still building it.
items.why: Present perfect continuous with since.

items.s: Lara last called me three weeks ago.
items.why: Present perfect negative + for + a period of time.

items.s: I will text you the moment I get to the airport.
items.why: As soon as means the moment that.

items.s: They cancelled the match because of the storm.
items.e: the match because of the storm.
items.why: Call off means cancel.

items.s: I cannot understand why he is so angry.
items.why: Work out or figure out means understand or solve.

items.s: Our plane left the ground at ten o'clock.
items.why: Take off means leave the ground.

items.s: I am looking after my neighbour's cat this week.
items.why: Take care of means look after.

items.s: We have no more coffee.
items.why: Run out of means use all of something.

items.s: He resembles his grandfather a lot.
items.why: Take after means resemble a family member.

items.s: Sara tolerates her brother's loud music without complaining.
items.e: her brother's loud music without complaining.
items.why: Put up with means tolerate.

items.s: Please complete this form before you leave.
items.why: Fill in or fill out a form.

items.s: My car stopped working on the motorway.
items.why: Break down means stop working.

items.s: We must try to reduce the amount of plastic we use.
items.e: the amount of plastic we use.
items.why: Cut down (on) or cut back on means reduce.

items.s: It is pointless to try to change her mind.
items.why: There is no point in + -ing.

items.s: He did not know that the film had already started.
items.e: that the film had already started.
items.why: Have no idea means not know.

items.s: Please be patient; it will only take a moment.
items.e: me; it will only take a moment.
items.why: Bear with me means please wait patiently.

items.s: Do not arrive late for the nine o'clock meeting.
items.why: On time means at the arranged time, not late.

items.s: I did not mean to break your phone.
items.b: I did not break your phone
items.why: On purpose means deliberately.

items.s: You must make the decision yourself.
items.why: It is up to you means it is your decision.

items.s: I think the new rules are unfair.
items.why: In my view means in my opinion.

items.s: We must decide quickly because we have almost no time left.
items.b: We must decide quickly because time
items.why: Time is running out means there is little time left.

items.s: I am not very interested in sport.
items.why: Interest in + noun.

items.s: The police suspect that he stole the paintings.
items.why: Suspect someone of + -ing.

items.s: The children were very excited about the trip.
items.why: Look forward to + noun.

items.s: You cannot rely on him because he never keeps his promises.
items.e: him because he never keeps his promises.
items.why: Depend on + noun.

items.s: Karen is fond of jazz.
items.why: Keen on + noun.

items.s: The flights were delayed because of the strike.
items.why: On account of means because of.

items.s: You can only enter the lab if you have a pass.
items.why: Unless means if not, so the verb after it is positive in form.

items.s: I would like to travel more, but I have not got enough money.
items.why: Second conditional: if + past simple.

items.s: We did not take a map, so we got lost.
items.e: a map, we would not have got lost.
items.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

items.s: She did not revise, so she failed the test.
items.why: Third conditional result clause: would have + past participle.

items.s: Take an umbrella because it may rain later.
items.why: In case + present simple, as a precaution.

items.s: You can borrow my laptop if you promise to be careful.
items.why: As long as means on condition that.

items.s: I do not know the answer, so I cannot tell you.
items.e: the answer, I would tell you.
items.why: Second conditional: if + past simple.

items.s: I would have failed without your help.
items.e: your help, I would have failed.
items.why: If it had not been for means without (third conditional).

items.s: Maybe it will rain, and then the match will be cancelled.
items.why: First conditional: if + present simple.

items.s: I would go to the party, but I am working tomorrow.
items.b: I would go to the party
items.why: Second conditional with be: were for all persons.

items.s: I regret not studying medicine at university.
items.why: Wish + past perfect for a regret about the past.

items.s: It is a pity you cannot come to the party.
items.why: Wish + could for something you want to be possible now.

items.s: I would prefer you not to smoke in here.
items.why: Would rather + someone + past simple for a present preference.

items.s: Tom is sorry that he did not apologise to Mia.
items.why: If only + past perfect expresses a strong regret.

items.s: I am annoyed that my neighbours play loud music every night.
items.why: Wish + would for an annoying habit.

items.s: You should go to bed now; it is late.
items.why: It is time + subject + past simple.

items.s: He regrets selling his guitar.
items.why: Wish + past perfect for a past regret.

items.s: She does not live near the sea, and she would love to.
items.why: Wish + past simple for an unreal present situation.

items.s: It is not necessary for you to bring any food.
items.why: Do not need to or need not: no obligation.

items.s: Perhaps he missed the bus.
items.why: May have + past participle: a possibility about the past.

items.s: It is impossible that Ellie took your keys because she was not here.
items.e: your keys because she was not here.
items.why: Cannot have + past participle: certain it did not happen.

items.s: It was wrong of you not to tell me earlier.
items.why: Should have + past participle: criticism of a past action.

items.s: It was not necessary for us to hurry because the train was late.
items.why: Did not need to + infinitive: it was not necessary.

items.s: I am sure that she is exhausted after the long trip.
items.why: Must + be for a logical deduction about the present.

items.s: Is it all right if I use your phone?
items.why: May I + infinitive: a polite request.

items.s: You are not allowed to park here.
items.why: Must not expresses a prohibition.

items.s: I think it would be a good idea for you to speak to your manager.
items.why: Had better + bare infinitive: strong advice.

items.s: Perhaps Jack will win the competition, but I doubt it.
items.e: the competition, but I doubt it.
items.why: Might + bare infinitive: a weak possibility.

items.s: She was able to swim when she was only three.
items.why: Could for general ability in the past.

items.s: I was forced to leave early because of the storm.
items.why: Had to for obligation in the past.

items.s: 'You've deleted my saved game, Leo!' said Maya.
items.why: accuse someone of + -ing.

items.s: My bike really needs to be fixed before the weekend.
items.why: get / have something done: someone else does it for you.

items.s: Lucas regrets not joining the school band.
items.why: wish + past perfect: a regret about the past.

items.s: I could never have finished the project if you hadn't helped me.
items.b: I could never have finished the project
items.why: without + someone + -ing replaces an if-clause.

items.s: I thought my phone battery might die, so I took a power bank.
items.b: I took a power bank with me
items.why: in case + past simple: a precaution.

items.s: The storm ruined our plans for a beach party.
items.b: Our plans for a beach party
items.why: fall through: fail to happen.

items.s: The bananas were too old to eat.
items.why: too + adjective = not + opposite adjective + enough.

items.s: Perhaps Sara left the party early.
items.why: may have + past participle: something possible in the past.

items.s: I can't possibly study with all this noise!
items.why: It is impossible (for someone) to + infinitive.

items.s: The player didn't realise the scouts were watching him.
items.b: The player didn't realise that he
items.why: past continuous passive: was being + past participle.

items.s: Who does this blue coat belong to?
items.why: whose + noun asks who something belongs to; the question becomes statement order.

items.s: Tom's ankle injury meant he couldn't play in the final.
items.why: prevent someone (from) + -ing.

items.s: Students are not allowed to use phones during the exam.
items.why: modal passive: must not be + past participle.

items.s: To Ana's amazement, the shop was already closed when she got there.
items.e: the shop already closed when she got there.
items.why: be amazed / surprised to find + something + adjective.

items.s: It isn't necessary to book tickets for the school concert.
items.why: don't need to / needn't: it isn't necessary.

items.s: The shelf was so high that my little brother couldn't reach it.
items.why: too + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive.

items.s: I'd prefer you to start the new project next week.
items.why: would rather + someone + past simple.

items.s: 'What do we have to do for homework?' the students asked the teacher.
items.why: reported question: statement word order, tense one step back.

items.s: Our coach almost never loses his temper.
items.why: hardly ever = almost never.

items.s: My phone has no battery left.
items.why: run out of: have none left.

items.s: There's no point asking Dan to help, because he's always busy.
items.e: Dan to help, because he's always busy.
items.why: it's not worth + -ing.

items.s: Mia's parents refused to allow her to get a tattoo.
items.why: let someone do: no to before the verb.

items.s: 'Where did you leave the charger?' Sam asked me.
items.why: reported question: tense one step back, no did.

items.s: Leo managed to finish the marathon.
items.why: succeed in + -ing.

items.s: You lent me the money, so I didn't have to go to the bank.
items.e: me the money, I would have had to go to the bank.
items.why: third conditional: if + had not + past participle.

items.s: Jack ignored the coach's advice.
items.why: take no notice of = ignore.

items.s: As well as tidying her room, Lily had to walk the dog.
items.b: Lily had to walk the dog
items.why: in addition to + -ing = as well as.

items.s: Marco went surfing almost every day while he was in Portugal.
items.b: Marco went surfing almost every day
items.why: during + noun phrase replaces while + clause.

items.s: Let's go to the cinema this evening.
items.why: Why don't we …? makes a suggestion.

items.s: Sam found it hard to concentrate because of the noise.
items.why: have difficulty (in) + -ing.

items.s: 'Emma should wait by the entrance,' said Leslie.
items.why: suggest (that) + someone + should + infinitive.

items.s: Although Clive overslept, he arrived at work on time.
items.why: despite + -ing; turn up = arrive.

items.s: I have never eaten sushi before.
items.why: This is the first time + present perfect.

items.s: After a long chase, the police caught the thief.
items.b: After a long chase, the police
items.why: manage to + infinitive: succeed in doing something difficult.

items.s: It was wrong of Diane not to call her grandmother last week.
items.why: ought to have + past participle: criticism of the past.

items.s: His handwriting is so small that I can hardly read it.
items.e: that I can hardly read it.
items.why: such + (adjective) + noun + that.

items.s: Someone must collect the visitors from the airport.
items.why: modal passive with a phrasal verb: must be picked up.

items.s: I'm sorry I told Max about the surprise party.
items.why: regret + -ing: sorry about something you did.

items.s: Everyone was surprised when Lena won the competition.
items.why: to everyone's surprise = everyone was surprised.

items.s: All the witnesses said the crash was my fault.
items.b: All the witnesses said that I
items.why: be to blame for = be responsible for.

items.s: Nobody has told us why our train is late.
items.why: the reason for + noun.

items.s: I'd rather you didn't text me during lessons.
items.why: would prefer someone not to + infinitive.

items.s: I had to save up for six months to buy my new console.
items.e: save up for my new console.
items.why: It took me + time + to + infinitive.

items.s: They are going to release the new trailer next Friday.
items.why: future passive: will be / is going to be + past participle.

items.s: 'Did you remember to feed the cat, Dad?' I asked.
items.why: reported yes/no question: if / whether + tense one step back.

items.s: We didn't expect to reach the final, but we trained hard anyway.
items.e: to reach the final, we trained hard anyway.
items.why: in spite of + -ing (the negative goes before the -ing).

items.s: I don't intend to tell anyone my password.
items.why: have no intention of + -ing.

items.s: You can decide where we eat tonight.
items.why: It's up to you (to decide) = you can choose.

items.s: Sasha only changed schools because her coach advised her to.
items.b: If her coach hadn't advised her to,
items.why: third conditional: would not have + past participle.

items.s: The fish tank needs cleaning once a week.
items.why: has to be + past participle = needs + -ing.

items.s: It would be hard for me to finish the poster by Monday.
items.why: have difficulty (in) + -ing.

items.s: Harry's home is still in Spain, isn't it?
items.why: the tag doesn't he? needs a present simple verb: lives.

items.s: When Carla arrived, she didn't say hello to anyone.
items.why: without + -ing = and didn't.

items.s: You can borrow my headphones if you need them.
items.e: you my headphones if you need them.
items.why: don't mind + -ing = I'm happy to.

items.s: Ana rarely misses a training session.
items.why: It is rare for someone to + infinitive.

items.s: We lost the match because I made a mistake.
items.why: It was my fault (that) + clause.

items.s: Are you doing anything special this weekend?
items.why: have plans for + time.

items.s: Ella looks nothing like her mother.
items.why: take after = look or behave like an older relative.

items.s: The book was better than the film.
items.why: not as + adjective + as = less than.

items.s: I regret showing Ollie my diary.
items.why: wish + past perfect: a regret about the past.

items.s: I'd rather not go to the party tonight.
items.why: not feel like + -ing = not want to.

items.s: I've never been to a concert as good as this before.
items.why: the best … I have ever + past participle.

items.s: All the players have great respect for their captain.
items.why: look up to = respect and admire.

items.s: 'Is there anything you need from the shop?' Alison asked her grandmother.
items.why: reported question: there is becomes there was.

items.s: Leo might forget his water bottle, so I'll bring two.
items.why: in case + present simple for a future possibility.

items.s: We got lost because we forgot to download a map.
items.e: a map, we wouldn't have got lost.
items.why: third conditional: if + had + past participle.

items.s: Tom was sure there were no mistakes in his code.
items.why: there is nothing wrong with = it has no mistakes.

items.s: Although the weather changed, the race went ahead.
items.why: in spite of + noun phrase.

items.s: I advise you to read the instructions before you start.
items.why: had better + infinitive: strong advice.

items.s: Jackie hasn't been skating for two years.
items.why: The last time + past simple + was … ago.

items.s: Martin hasn't mentioned the trip to me at all.
items.why: not say a word = not mention at all.

items.s: It seems that the shop is closed today.
items.why: appear to + infinitive = seem.

items.s: Margaret was offered a place in the team but couldn't accept because she was injured.
items.b: Margaret was offered a place in the team but had to
items.why: turn down = refuse an offer.

items.s: 'I wouldn't trust that website if I were you, Carl,' I said.
items.why: advise someone not to + infinitive.

items.s: I don't know why Lesley left the club.
items.why: have no idea = don't know.

items.s: Have you got any phone cases cheaper than this one?
items.why: the + superlative + noun.

items.s: Teams of engineers were checking the damage to the bridge.
items.why: past continuous passive: was being + past participle + by.

items.s: Joe's mum used to insist that he tidied his room every Saturday.
items.why: make someone do: no to.

items.s: I wish my cousin still sent me postcards.
items.why: miss + -ing: be sad that something no longer happens.

items.s: Everyone thinks Alan will accept the job offer.
items.why: is expected to + infinitive: what people think will happen.

items.s: 'Would you like a table by the window?' the waiter asked us.
items.e: to have a table by the window.
items.why: reported question: if + we would.

items.s: I'm bored here, so let's go somewhere else.
items.why: Why don't we …? makes a suggestion.

items.s: I really didn't want to queue for tickets, so I bought them online.
items.e: for tickets, so I bought them online.
items.why: avoid + -ing.

items.s: I couldn't decide between the black trainers and the white ones.
items.e: the black trainers and the white ones.
items.why: make a choice between = decide between.

items.s: Despite his disappointment, Max stayed cheerful.
items.why: although + clause; remain = stay.

items.s: There were so many people on the bus that I couldn't sit down.
items.why: so + adjective + that.

items.s: The tickets cost less than I had expected.
items.why: not as much as = less than.

items.s: My sister never watches TV before she has finished her homework.
items.b: My sister always finishes her homework
items.why: before + -ing.

items.s: My dad stopped smoking last year.
items.why: give up = stop doing a habit.

items.s: We last went camping three years ago.
items.why: It is / has been + time + since + past simple.

items.s: The school year finished with a big concert.
items.e: school year, there was a big concert.
items.why: at the end of + noun.

items.s: Be careful or you'll fall off your skateboard.
items.why: if + present simple for a warning about the future.

items.s: Finding a cheap hotel in summer might be difficult.
items.why: It might be + adjective + to + infinitive.

items.s: The price of the school trip includes all meals.
items.e: the price of the school trip.
items.why: passive: are included in.

items.s: In my opinion, the problem has two causes.
items.why: there are + number + noun.

items.s: 'Don't forget to bring your PE kit,' the teacher told me.
items.why: remind someone to + infinitive.

items.s: You're cycling too fast for me!
items.why: keep up with = go as fast as.

items.s: Where can I find the bus station?
items.why: how to + infinitive in an indirect question.

items.s: Mary used to earn more than she does now.
items.why: not as much as = less than.

items.s: I'm happy to watch any film you choose.
items.why: It doesn't matter (to me) which … = I don't mind.

items.s: We took a train to Lisbon last summer.
items.why: by + transport, with no article.

items.s: Mark left the party and didn't thank us for inviting him.
items.why: without + -ing = and didn't.

items.s: We are hoping that the weather will improve for the match.
items.why: hope for + noun.

items.s: Who has to switch off the lights after the show?
items.why: be responsible for + -ing.

items.s: I was really pleased that my brother had finally managed to pass his driving test.
items.b: I was really pleased that my brother had finally
items.why: be successful in + -ing = manage to.

items.s: I went to sleep immediately after the film started.
items.why: fall asleep; as soon as = immediately after.

items.s: It's unlikely that I'll see you again before the holidays.
items.why: probably goes after will but before won't.

items.s: It will be great to see you again at the festival.
items.why: look forward to + -ing.

items.s: I haven't forgotten any of the details of my first concert.
items.why: still remember = haven't forgotten.

items.s: We got lost because the signs were confusing.
items.why: cause someone to + infinitive.

items.s: She didn't buy the jacket because it was too expensive.
items.b: She would have bought the jacket
items.why: third conditional: if + had not been.

items.s: He sold his old games to earn some extra money.
items.why: in order to + infinitive: purpose.

items.s: My gran thinks that people who scroll on their phones all day are wasting their time.
items.b: My gran thinks scrolling on your phone all day
items.why: be a waste of time.

items.s: You won't have to come to practice next week.
items.e: to come to practice next week.
items.why: It will not be necessary (for you) to = you won't have to.

items.s: My friend didn't expect the show to be so funny.
items.why: comparative + than: funnier than expected.

items.s: Martin needs his glasses to read the timetable.
items.why: without + -ing.

items.s: Alan's children behave badly, so nobody invites them to parties any more.
items.e: nobody invites them to parties any more.
items.why: which is why = and for this reason.

items.s: It was fortunate that Ben wasn't hurt in the fall.
items.why: be lucky (not) to + infinitive.

items.s: Rita is the only person in our class who likes maths tests.
items.why: apart from = except.

items.s: I didn't think that Peter would call tonight.
items.why: be unlikely to + infinitive.

items.s: Gaming doesn't interest my brother at all.
items.why: be interested in + noun.

items.s: Visitors to the museum are not allowed to take photos.
items.why: be prohibited = not be allowed.

items.s: Kate had never been to Madeira before.
items.why: someone's first visit to + place.

items.s: 'I'll see you after school, Anna,' he said.
items.why: reported speech: will becomes would.

items.s: There were fewer fans at the match this year than last year.
items.e: at the match this year as last year.
items.why: not as many + plural noun + as = fewer than.

items.s: When I was in the shop, someone thought I was the manager.
items.b: When I was in the shop, someone
items.why: mistake someone for = wrongly think they are someone else.

items.s: I wonder how she learnt to play the piano so well.
items.e: know how she learnt to play the piano so well.
items.why: would like to know = I wonder.

items.s: Although Dan can't swim, he loves sailing.
items.why: despite + being + adjective.

items.s: I'm sure our team won't lose tomorrow.
items.why: there is no chance of + -ing.

items.s: It's lucky you called, or we wouldn't have known about the change.
items.e: called, we wouldn't have known about the change.
items.why: third conditional: if + had not + past participle.

items.s: Ana was the only person who didn't laugh at the joke.
items.why: except for = apart from.

items.s: They're going to knock down the old cinema.
items.b: The old cinema is going to
items.why: passive with a phrasal verb: be pulled down.

items.s: My sister started learning Japanese three years ago.
items.why: present perfect continuous + for: still happening.

items.s: 'Don't touch the paintings, Leo!' said the guide.
items.why: tell someone not to + infinitive.

items.s: The trip to Porto was cheaper than I had expected.
items.why: not as + adjective + as.

items.s: My phone was so badly damaged that I didn't try to repair it.
items.b: My phone was so badly damaged that there
items.why: there is no point in + -ing.

items.s: I expect you were exhausted after the tournament.
items.why: must have been: you are sure about the past.

items.s: It was unfair that the skater was given such low marks.
items.why: not deserve to be + past participle.

items.s: There's no juice in this carton.
items.why: there is nothing left = it is empty.

items.s: My aunt didn't learn to drive until she was forty.
items.why: not until = only when; finally adds the idea of late.

items.s: I haven't seen my cousin since he moved to Australia.
items.e: my cousin was before he moved to Australia.
items.why: The last time + past simple.

items.s: The price of the course includes all the books.
items.why: cover the cost of = include the price of.

items.s: 'You should have asked me before you borrowed my bike,' Tom said to his son.
items.b: Tom criticised his son for borrowing his bike
items.why: without + -ing.

items.s: You ought to get your bike brakes repaired immediately.
items.why: had better + get something done.

items.s: Sarah is not usually late.
items.why: It's not like someone to … = it's unusual for them.

items.s: I'd prefer nobody else to know about my surprise party plans.
items.why: not want anyone else to + infinitive.

items.s: They cancelled the concert because of the storm.
items.why: owing to = because of.

items.s: I left early because I didn't want to miss the bus.
items.why: so that + would not: purpose.

items.s: The teacher spoke so fast that we couldn't understand her.
items.why: too + adverb + for someone + to.

items.s: The coach said I could miss training on Friday.
items.why: give someone permission to + infinitive.

items.s: I didn't know you were ill, so I didn't send you a message.
items.b: If I'd known you were ill, I
items.why: third conditional: would have + past participle.

items.s: After the hike, Lucy was so tired that she couldn't stay awake.
items.why: too + adjective + to + infinitive.

items.s: I can't stand your messy room any more.
items.why: put up with = accept something annoying.

items.s: Could you lend me your surfboard?
items.why: Would you mind + -ing? is a polite request.

items.s: My parents didn't let me stay out late when I was twelve.
items.e: out late when I was twelve.
items.why: be (not) allowed to = be (not) let.

items.s: How long was your flight from Lisbon to London?
items.why: How long does it take (you) to + infinitive?

items.s: The last time I went bowling was two years ago.
items.why: present perfect + for = since the last time.

items.s: Rui bought the new phone in spite of not really needing it.
items.why: although + clause = in spite of + -ing.

items.s: Teenagers aren't buying as many CDs these days.
items.why: present continuous passive: are being + past participle.

items.s: I regret telling everyone my secret.
items.why: wish + past perfect: a regret about the past.
